issues.failure_explanation: Summing the cellwise identity over all K leaves, besides the t=0, t=T and jump faces, the outer faces on ∂Ω×(0,T); their integrand (F(u_θ*)−F(ũ_h))sgn(u_θ*−ũ_h)·n does not vanish, because supp u⊂Ω forces u=0 near ∂Ω but imposes nothing on the tanh network u_θ*. Hence the displayed identity (and its analogues) is false and the stability estimate acquires an uncontrolled boundary flux. The loss cannot control it: for f(u)=u any smooth solution of ∂_t v+∂_x v=0 with v(·,0)=u_0 that injects mass through ∂Ω has ∇·F(v)=0 in Ω_T, so L_ent=L_bc=L_reg=0 while ‖v(·,T)−u(·,T)‖_{L^1}=O(1).

issues.failure_explanation: thm:shock_interaction is stated under Assumption assump:piecewise_smooth but proved only by invoking thm:more_general_case, which assumes the different Assumption assump:shock_3d. A terminal-time interaction satisfies neither: the incoming shocks meet only at (x_β,T)∉Ω_T, so Γ_i∩Γ_j=∅ inside Ω_T while dist(Γ_1,Γ_2)=0, contradicting the separation condition dist(S_1,S_2)≥c_sep δ for all δ≤r_0, and the Γ_i are not compact in Ω_T. Conversely assump:piecewise_smooth(iii) requires an outgoing shock curve inside the event piece, which cannot exist when the interaction occurs at t=T. The delegated proof therefore applies outside its hypotheses and the stated class of solutions is empty as written.

failure_location.quote: A complete argument is contained in the proof of the more general higher-dimensional interaction result, Theorem~\ref{thm:more_general_case}; the present statement is a special case of that theorem.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Amend the assumptions to admit events on the terminal boundary (outgoing curve outside Ω_T, separation/transversality truncated at t=T) and supply the local surgery analysis at (x_β,T) in that degenerate geometry, or restrict the statement to interactions strictly before T and treat the terminal case separately.
issues.overall_effect: The O(h^{1/2}) estimate for solutions whose two shocks interact exactly at t=T is unproved; thm:main_1d, whose proof uses 'the local construction as in Theorem~\ref{thm:shock_interaction}' for interaction pieces, inherits the gap.

issues.failure_explanation: Below t=t_h the test function interpolates u (trace u⁻ there), while above t=t_h and to the right of the artificial interface Γ_j it interpolates the one-sided extension u_ext⁺≈u⁺. Since Γ_j lies up to O(Mh) left of the true shock, ũ_h jumps by |[u]| across the mesh faces on the horizontal line t=t_h between Γ_j and ∂E_h, a segment of length O(Mh). The claimed jump set is wrong and the error identity (eq:shock_birth_error_identity) omits this interface integral.

issues.failure_explanation: S_{min,τ}(r,s)=(r+s)/2−(r−s)tanh(τ(r−s))/2 contains the product of the affine quantity (r−s) with tanh(τ(r−s)); a network of the form eq:def:NN (affine layers composed with componentwise tanh) computes no products exactly, so the smoothed nodal hats φ_{j,τ} are not tanh networks with the quoted size. Approximating each min/max node by an auxiliary tanh subnetwork forces the width/depth to depend on ε=Θ(h²), so the ε-independent O(NN_patch)=O(h^{-(d+1)}) neuron and nonzero-parameter counts are unsupported.

issues.overall_effect: All statements that fix a network class of depth O(d+1) and width O(h^{-(d+1)}) neurons (lem:loss_cpwl_approx, the competitor lemmas and every error theorem) and the advertised O(h^{-(d+1)}) parameter count of rem:parameter_count and the abstract are unestablished; the loss bounds and the L^1 rates for a suitably sized class are not affected.

issues.why_classification: The loss estimates and all L^1 rates survive once the min–max nodes are realized approximately, but this requires a new approximation construction and weakens the stated O(h^{-(d+1)}) size bound; that is more than a local edit yet far short of losing the results.
